## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `710841dae1332f5c05286fc87dbf905ad539d9be`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md + none
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #36775 (card #36419), reviewed against merge-base `70f454a23cc7a6dbdd6ae3456a9d1475e10895d5` (origin/main at review time). The diff is two files: `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` (governed, the one `hits` path) and `.changeset/36419-skills-field-history-default.md` (prose face, read for ② only). Read with `git diff` / `git show` and the REST API; nothing was built or run.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- **N1 (nit):** the `fieldHistory` row says a media or structured field shows values "only with `true`". `resolveFieldHistory` also accepts the field's older `trackHistory: true`. The row teaches the current spelling, as the field schema's own description does; an agent following it writes valid metadata. Accepted as written.
- **N2 (nit):** the `aiReadable` row no longer says what the flag does (read-only AI access to a platform object's records) or that `sys_metadata` and `sys_metadata_history` are excluded. No other file under `skills/` states it. An app author cannot declare the key at all, and the row still says so, so no app-authoring rule changed. Accepted deviation; the schema description still carries the detail.
- **N3 (nit):** the `Security-touching` line reads `yes` because the new row teaches who is served a value, the credential rule and the ledger's grant, and the `sharingModel` row was edited. The PR stays at Tier H for the maintainer's own merge.

### ① Derived judgments

The two new rows, clause by clause, against `main`:

| Clause in the skill | Source on `main` | Holds |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `fieldHistory` default "on" | `object.zod.ts:366`, optional with no `.default()`; absent means values show. `resolveFieldHistory` returns true unless a rule below turns it off | yes |
| old → new values on the activity timeline | `field-history-default.ts` header; `object.zod.ts:351-366` (`sys_activity` stream) | yes |
| `false`: off for the object | `resolveFieldHistory` line 1: `object.enable.fieldHistory === false` returns false before any field flag is read | yes |
| a field opts out with its own `fieldHistory: false` | `resolveFieldHistory` line 2; `field.zod.ts:2767` | yes |
| media or structured field (`json`, `address`, `code`…) shows values only with `true` | `FIELD_HISTORY_DEFAULT_OFF_TYPES`: image, file, avatar, video, audio, signature, composite, repeater, record, location, address, code, json, vector; opt-in is a literal `true` | yes (see N1) |
| a credential never | `isMaskedOnReadFieldType` is tested before the opt-in line, so `true` cannot turn it on; `secret` always, `password` except on a `better-auth` object, which an app author does not write | yes |
| served per the reader's field read rule | `plugin-audit/src/activity-field-redaction.ts`: each change of a field the reader is not served is dropped at read time, through the security service | yes |
| `sys_audit_log` keeps its own grant | `plugin-audit/src/audit-log-read-visibility.ts`: the ledger is read under its own object grant, then narrowed to readable records | yes |
| `trackHistory` default `false` | `object.zod.ts:348`, `.default(false)` | yes |
| ledger view on the record page and the `history` API verb | `object.zod.ts:361-362`; `LEGACY_API_METHOD_GUIDANCE.history`: "derives from get ∧ trackHistory" | yes |
| not the values switch | `object.zod.ts:363`: an object writing `trackHistory: false` alone shows values | yes |

Card correction 7079973891 (the per-field off switch is `fieldHistory: false`, not `trackHistory: false`) is followed. `field.zod.ts:2754` confirms that a field's `trackHistory: false` is not an off switch.

Does any sentence left in `skills/objectstack-data/**` still teach opt-in? No. A search of the head tree for `trackHistory`, `fieldHistory`, `history` and `audit` finds:

- `SKILL.md:110-111`, the two rewritten rows.
- `references/examples-objects.md:67`, `enable.trackHistory: true` in the quick-start object. It carries no comment and makes no claim about values. The flag is still valid for the ledger view.
- `evals/objects-fields-relationships.json:289`, a `must_not_contain` entry on the sealed-ledger case. It is unrelated to the default.
- `SKILL.md:309` and `rules/lifecycle.md`, which speak of approval trails and `lifecycle.class: 'audit'`, not field history.

The twelve trimmed phrases, each checked for lost meaning or a changed rule:

| # | Row or sentence | Cut | Rule changed |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `sharingModel` | "— absence is not a decision" | no; "refused" and "Author it on every object" stay, and `references/lint-rules.md:22` keeps the phrase |
| 2 | posture paragraph | "not by habit" | no |
| 3 | `label` | "Human-readable" | no |
| 4 | `datasource` | "for virtualized data" | no; the spec says "Target Datasource ID", so the row is now closer to it |
| 5 | `nameField` | "**Canonical**" | no; the next row still names `displayNameField` as the deprecated alias |
| 6 | `fieldGroups` | "list of logical" | no |
| 7 | `lifecycle` default | "semantics" | no |
| 8 | `files` | "& document management" | no; the spec describes an attachments panel |
| 9 | `feeds` | "Social", "**opt-out**: explicit" | no; default `true` and the effect of `false` stay |
| 10 | `activities` | "**opt-out**: explicit" | no; same |
| 11 | search paragraph | ", not silently dropped" | no; "**refused**" with both codes stays |
| 12 | mirror paragraph | "a mirror is only as fresh as whatever writes it" | no; both hook paths and the backfill stay |

The `aiReadable` row is the thirteenth cut, named apart in the PR body; see N2. No eval under `skills/objectstack-data/evals/` asserts any removed phrase.

Ceiling: `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is not in the diff, so no ceiling moved. The row at head still reads `['skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md', 6710]`. By the script's own formula, `ceil((bytes - 20) / 4)`, read off the git objects: base 26843 bytes gives 6706, head 26854 bytes gives 6709. Lines are 471 on both. That is 6709 of 6710, as the PR states.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` is right. `packages/skills` publishes the skills tree; the change is wording only and adds no shape. Every earlier skill-wording changeset on `main` is a patch for the same package. The changeset carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, matching the PR body. `Clause-②: no` holds: no route, contract, spec key or export is added.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev report has no `open_questions`.
- Out-of-scope flag, class a: two shipped refusal texts in `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (the `enable.trash` guidance near line 212 and the `versioning` guidance near line 1950) still send an author to per-field `trackHistory` for field-level history. Confirmed on `main`. It is correctly left out of this PR, since editing it would open the published-schema face. No card carries it yet; the seat owes one.
- Noted flag: the card's "admin only" wording for the ledger was not copied into the skill. That is right. `audit-log-read-visibility.ts` serves the ledger under its own grant, which is what the row says, and the row names no audience.
- SQL push-down: no code in the diff, nothing to check.
- The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no separate author to name.
- The PR does not touch `.claude/**` and its body declares no `Rule-change:` line. No hunk changes what an agent may do without the maintainer, so the line above reads `none`.

Check-runs at the head, read at 2026-11-23T21:06Z: 19 success, 16 skipped, 6 still in progress, none failed. In progress: Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Test Core (1/10), Test Core (2/10). Lint · repo and tooling gates finished green during the review. The landing check for an all-green head is therefore not yet met. This record does not stand in for it, and the token-ratchet reading above is arithmetic from the git objects until the lint jobs report.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`: the change holds against the spec it teaches. An agent asked to "keep a change history on this object" now reads that values already show, and reaches for `enable.fieldHistory: false` or a field's `fieldHistory: false` only to turn them off. That is the contract #36399 landed. Splitting the fact into two rows mirrors the schema's own two keys and keeps `trackHistory` honest about what it still does. The row also answers the card's item 2 (who sees the values) in one clause without naming an audience the code does not enforce. Paying for the new text inside the same file, with the ceiling untouched, follows the ratchet's standing rule: cut repetition first.

Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbZeHNsF3RWcWpj7rGj`

**VERDICT: PASS**
